Take two equal and well polished round pieces of flat glass; upon the surface of one of which, all round its limb, glue a pasteboard ring: then put the other piece of glass into the smoke of a lamp, taking it several times out, and putting it in again, left the heat should break it, until the smoke be so thick, that the lamp can scarcely be seen through it: but the smoke must not be all over of the same thickness, that so a place may be chosen answering to the splendour of the sun.
